# Derek Kaneshiro

> Personal site of Derek Kaneshiro, an AI-native product engineer. Builds products end to end
> with AI in every phase: two full-stack products launched as a single engineer, the open-source
> AI evaluation framework Synthetic Test Fabric, and ten years owning a HIPAA-regulated clinical
> platform serving 500,000+ patients.

## About

Derek Kaneshiro is an AI-native product engineer based in Hillsboro, Oregon. As a single
engineer he built and launched two full-stack products, BlueSkil and Redy, each with a mobile
app, a web app, an API, a CLI and an MCP server. Narrow AI agents handle the recurring work
(tests, code review, schema validation, deploy gating), architecture lives in versioned context
files reviewed like code, and every deploy is gated on measured behavior.

Before this he spent ten years as principal engineer on the platform behind Zimmer Biomet's
orthopedic recovery products — a HIPAA-regulated system serving 500,000+ patients — building
the rules engine behind every patient's daily care plan and leading the R&D that carried the
first LLM prototypes through security and risk review.

He is looking for a product-engineer role, full-time or a scoped engagement, on a small team
that builds with AI in how the work gets done.

## Work

- BlueSkil — career platform matching skilled workers with verified employers; explainable
  AI matching and an MCP connection to Claude and ChatGPT. Publicly released. https://blueskil.com
- Redy — supplier-evidence workflow for EU Digital Product Passports. Publicly released.
  https://redy.co
- Synthetic Test Fabric — open-source evaluation framework for AI-built software (MIT, on NPM).
  Ships fab-mcp, an MCP server. https://github.com/kaneshir/synthetic-test-fabric
- Toknize — in active development.
